transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Sunday, October 25. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Protests sweep France, Spain as masked mobs loot shops, clash with cops; 1,100 held. Videos shared online showed people trapped inside shops, including the department store El Corte Ingles, after shutters were lowered to prevent looting. Other footage showed hooded demonstrators dressed in black smashing shop windows and taking goods, sometimes encouraged by people watching online. Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni warned that acts of vandalism "will not go unpunished". 'Prioritise welfare over military directives': India raps Pak on minority rights. Speaking at an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Minority Issues at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission to the UN, Raghoo Puri, called out Pakistan's conduct and said its representatives should focus on the welfare of their own people instead of taking directions from the military. Drawn in same group, IND-PAK set to clash on Nov 22 in Rising Asia Cup. India A will open their campaign against Nepal on November 20 before taking on Pakistan A two days later. They will play their final group-stage match against the UAE on November 24. No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that "right given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do so". Michael and Susan Dell's foundation spotlights free skills training in Texas. The Michael and Susan Dell Foundation has reported remarkable achievements among graduates of its skilled-trades training initiatives. Over a dedicated five-week course crafted with input from employers, participants secure jobs almost immediately. Success stories like Mariah showcase a transition into well-paying, stable careers, while Skillpoint Alliance is enhancing training capacities to address Texas's rising need for skilled workers, ultimately promoting economic growth and assisting businesses in meeting workforce challenges. Farooq Abdullah's comments on Pakistan and Kashmir draw flak. Farooq urged NC workers and legislators to remain loyal to the party, whether in power or not, as he touched on a range of issues in his speech. "Hold on to the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you remain truthful and stand up for what is right, your future will never be secure," the veteran said. Helen Mirren fights to save Italy's 1,500-year-old olives after 22m trees lost. Helen Mirren, 81, is fighting to save Italy's ancient olive trees from Xylella fastidiosa, a deadly bacterium that has reportedly destroyed around 22 million trees since 2013. Through her initiative, Save the Olives, the Oscar winner is supporting conservation efforts and developing resistant varieties. "We have to save these trees," she says. 'Saddam Hussein opened a cheesecake factory': Obama's jibe at Trump's White House. Former US President Barack Obama took a dig at Donald Trump over his renovation plans for the White House, saying Trump has "got the White House looking like former Iraq President Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory". New York court revives privacy claim over cameras filming family's backyard. A couple in New York found themselves entangled in a complex property disagreement with their neighbors regarding a disputed land boundary tied to a chain-link fence. This conflict escalated, resulting in claims of trespassing and invasion of privacy due to surveillance cameras. Although the court struggled to rule on the boundary dispute, it has permitted the couple's privacy claims to advance for further scrutiny. Rocket Mortgage founder turns $1 billion Detroit pledge into nonprofit fund. Billionaire Dan Gilbert announces a remarkable $1 billion investment aimed at revitalizing Detroit's Renaissance Center and nearby riverfront. This project will be overseen by a nonprofit organization that emphasizes community benefits with no profits going to Gilbert. The plan includes the creation of modern housing and a vibrant walkable district complete with parks and entertainment venues.
